title: introduce-deconvolutional-drift-prober-and-soft-failover-policy
author: Maya S. Park
description: Motivation: intermittent, slowly accumulating latency regressions in mixed-traffic environments were frequently masked by aggregated canary signals. This PR introduces a deconvolutional drift prober that separates correlated traffic covariates (request size, concurrency, model variant mix, and input modality) from true per-replica latency drift and pairs it with a soft-failover policy that reduces blast radius without an immediate hard rollback. Approach: add a canary evaluator plugin (deconv_drift_prober) that runs lightweight deconvolution on streaming telemetry, computes per-covariate residuals, and emits a probabilistic drift score. The soft-failover policy uses a hysteresis-backed traffic-weighted throttling action that progressively shifts traffic away from affected replicas and falls back to a compatible model variant only after a sustained confidence threshold. Configuration: new canary config fields deconv_window_seconds, covariate_list, residual_threshold, soft_failover_grace_seconds, and max_shift_pct. The feature is guarded behind runtime flag canary.deconv_prober.enabled and is off by default. Tests: unit tests for the deconvolutional estimator, integration tests in perf-canary harness with synthetic traffic patterns (burst, diurnal, phased model skew), and a canary E2E job that validates no false-positive rollbacks on 10k-sample windows. Rollout plan: opt-in in staging for two weeks using traffic shadowing, then gradual enable on canaries for low-traffic namespaces with observability dashboards; monitor false-positive rate and rollback frequency via new metric canary.deconv.false_positives. Related work: builds on ENG-3629 (covariate-normalized canary baseline) and complements ENG-3680 (traffic-aware probe scheduler). Checklist: ensure feature flag gating, docs updated, metrics exported, perf unit tests added, runbook note written. Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing canary schemas when feature flag off.

review_comments: Alex Ruiz: Nice approach. Can you justify the choice of deconvolution algorithm and its O(n) runtime under high concurrency? Suggest adding a microbenchmark in perf_harness.
Maya S. Park: Added a microbenchmark and included its results in perf_harness.yml. The algorithm uses incremental least-squares with L2 regularization to be streaming-friendly.
Priya Nambiar: We should ensure this doesn't increase tail latency by running the prober on a dedicated worker pool. Please add option to run in-process vs out-of-process.
Maya S. Park: Added config flag prober.execution_mode with choices inproc|worker-pool and updated docs; default is worker-pool for production.
Evan Cho: CI flaked on the integration test due to timing; reran CI and all checks passed. Approve after addressing minor logging message formatting.
Maya S. Park: Fixed logging format and pushed the change. CI green.
ci_summary: Initial CI run: tests failed due to a flaky integration timing assumption; updated harness and reran. Final CI: all unit, integration, lint, and perf smoke checks passed. Coverage delta: +1.8% in canary package.
merge_outcome: merged via squash on 2025-02-22 by Alex Ruiz using commit message 'deconv: add drift prober and soft failover (ENG-3629, ENG-3680)'
release_notes: Add deconvolutional canary prober to improve detection of covariate-driven latency drift
Introduce soft-failover policy that gradually shifts traffic to limit blast radius
New config fields: deconv_window_seconds, residual_threshold, soft_failover_grace_seconds, prober.execution_mode
Feature is behind runtime flag canary.deconv_prober.enabled (off by default)
